title: The Lebenswelt and the Shire: Frankfurt Social Theory, Palantir, and the Wartime Chief Executive
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: New York City, the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp), as are both parents' names and occupations: Robert Joseph Karp, a Jewish clinical pediatrician, and Leah Jaynes Karp, an African American artist. No hospital and no borough is named in any source consulted, so the pin is city-level. No source explains the middle name Caedmon; the gloss on the seventh-century poet is offered as the name's meaning, not as the family's stated reason. A dossier detail giving his mother an interest in Korean art and language is not carried: no reachable source supports it.
stops.campa: Alexander Caedmon Karp is born on the second of October to Robert Joseph Karp, a Jewish clinical pediatrician, and Leah Jaynes Karp, an African American artist. The middle name is Anglo-Saxon and belongs to the seventh-century cowherd of Whitby who woke with the gift of song. Thirty-five years later he will hang that name on a money-management firm in London. No hospital is named in the record and no borough. What survives of the day is the date, the two parents and their occupations, and the childhood happens in Philadelphia.
suggested_refs: Caedmon of Whitby, the illiterate cowherd given the gift of English verse in Bede's Historia Ecclesiastica

stops.name: Philadelphia, the household of protest
stops.date_confidence: the household and the parents' activism are attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp: he was influenced by his parents' activism for civil rights and social justice during his youth and went to many protests). The 1970 date is an editorial placement to open the Philadelphia childhood; no source dates any particular march, and the detail is substantially Karp's own recollection.
stops.campa: The family settles in Philadelphia and the boy grows up between two histories the country keeps in separate rooms. His father is a clinical pediatrician, his mother an artist, and both are political people; the marches for civil rights and social justice are not a subject in the house but an afternoon in it, with the child taken along. He says later that his politics were made there. He is still saying it forty years on, to rooms full of people who assume a man who sells software to armies cannot mean it. The account of the childhood is largely his own.

stops.name: Philadelphia, the letters that will not sit still
stops.date_confidence: the dyslexia is attested as a repeated self-report (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp: he said he struggled with dyslexia from an early age). No source dates a diagnosis or an onset to any year; a dossier chronology giving 1975 is invented and is not followed. The 1976 date is a placement inside the Philadelphia childhood and carries no claim. No medical record has been made public. The quote is from 2025 and is placed here for what it describes, not for when it was said.
stops.campa: He is dyslexic. The account is his own and he gives it constantly: reading comes hard, school is a fight conducted in a language that will not sit still on the page, and the boy learns to hold an argument in his head instead, where the words stay where he puts them. There is no diagnosis on record and no document of any kind, only the telling. What survives is the habit it built. He is in his fifties when he describes that habit, still, as an advantage.
stops.quote: I'm attenuated to the taxonomy so the taxonomy doesn't become me. And that attenuation is crazy valuable when you're trying to do something that is unique because I don't have that.
stops.quote_source: Economic Club of New York, fireside chat transcript, 24 February 2025 (econclubny.org, official transcript PDF)
sources: Economic Club of New York transcript, 24 February 2025

stops.name: Central High School, the graduation
stops.date_confidence: graduation in 1985 is attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp); the month is a default. Coordinates are 1700 West Olney Avenue per en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_High_School_(Philadelphia); the school has occupied that campus since 1937, so the 1985 building is this one. A dossier pin at 40.0294, -75.1517 is about 900 m off and is not used. Nothing is recorded about his coursework or performance there.
stops.campa: He graduates from Central High School, Philadelphia's selective public magnet, which admits by examination and has stood on its West Olney Avenue campus since 1937. A boy who describes reading as a fight takes a diploma from a school nobody enters without passing a test. He is seventeen. Ten miles west, across the county line, a Quaker college will take him for four years of philosophy. What he studied at Central, who taught him, how he did: the record gives the year of the diploma and nothing else.
suggested_refs: Central High School, Philadelphia, 1700 West Olney Avenue

segments.name: Haverford and Stanford: The Argument Begins

stops.name: Haverford College, philosophy among the Quakers
stops.date_confidence: the B.A. in philosophy from Haverford in 1989 is attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp); the September 1985 matriculation is a default placement of the four-year span. That Michael Steinberger was a Haverford classmate is attested independently (kirkusreviews.com, review of The Philosopher in the Valley, which calls him a Haverford College classmate). Classmates' recollections of Karp as intensely argumentative and drawn to Marxist theory are dossier colour and remain unverified; haverford.edu returned 403 on every attempt.
stops.campa: He crosses the county line to Haverford, a small Quaker-founded college where he reads philosophy for four years and takes the degree in 1989. Classmates remember an argumentative left-winger, though that is recollection and not record. One of them, Michael Steinberger, will watch him from a distance for thirty-six years and then write the first substantial biography of him, published in 2025 as The Philosopher in the Valley: Alex Karp, Palantir, and the Rise of the Surveillance State.
suggested_refs: Michael Steinberger, The Philosopher in the Valley (Avid Reader Press, November 2025), by a Haverford classmate
sources: kirkusreviews.com, review of The Philosopher in the Valley

stops.name: Stanford Law School, the socialist and the libertarian
stops.date_confidence: attested that Karp and Peter Thiel were fellow students at Stanford Law School and that the arguments between them, Karp as self-described socialist and Thiel as libertarian capitalist, began there and outlasted the degree (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Thiel). No source dates the meeting; 1990 orders the three law-school years. Coordinates are inherited byte-identical from peter_thiel.journey.json, stop 'Stanford Law School, the J.D. and The Diversity Myth'.
stops.campa: He goes west to Stanford Law School and meets Peter Thiel there, in the same graduating class, in the same small building. What begins is not a friendship built on agreement. Karp argues socialism; Thiel argues capitalism and the liberty of the individual against the crowd; each is pleased to have found somebody who will not concede. The argument outlasts law school by more than thirty years and survives a company, a war and a presidency. Neither of them has reported winning it.
sources: peter_thiel.journey.json, stop 'Stanford Law School, the J.D. and The Diversity Myth'

stops.name: Stanford Law School, the J.D. and the step off the ladder
stops.date_confidence: the 1992 J.D. is attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp); month and day are defaults, June following the convention used in peter_thiel.journey.json for the same degree. That he never practiced law is inferred from the absence of any bar admission, firm, or clerkship in any reachable source, and is carried as reconstruction. The years between 1992 and his arrival in Frankfurt are an honest gap: no source consulted accounts for them.
stops.campa: He takes the J.D. in 1992 and never practices. No firm, no clerkship, no bar: the last rung of a conventional ladder, and he steps off it. What he does for the next two or three years is not documented in anything reachable, which is worth recording, because nearly every other year of this life is. Two or three years of a documented man go missing between the degree and the next thing. When he surfaces he is in Germany, studying social theory in a language he does not speak.

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, arrival without the language
stops.date_confidence: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp and de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp agree that he lived in Frankfurt from the mid-1990s until 2001 and considered staying permanently. A dossier chronology giving a 1994 arrival is earlier than either encyclopedia supports and is not followed; c.1995 is the earliest defensible date and month and day are defaults. That he arrived without German is from the legrandcontinent.eu interview with Karola Brede, fetched, and is her recollection. Coordinates are the Bockenheim site of Goethe University and the Institut fur Sozialforschung, inherited byte-identical from jurgen_habermas.journey.json, stop 'Frankfurt, Bockenheim, Horkheimer's chair'; the university's Westend campus in the IG Farben building did not open to the humanities until 2001.
stops.campa: He arrives in Frankfurt am Main without German and begins, at twenty-seven, to build a second intellectual life inside a second language. The city he picks is not neutral ground: the Institute for Social Research on the Senckenberganlage is where the critical theory of the century was made, unmade in exile, and brought back after the war. He will spend roughly six years here and seriously consider staying for good. The dissertation, when it comes, will be written in German and has never been translated.
suggested_refs: The Institut fur Sozialforschung, Senckenberganlage, Frankfurt
sources: legrandcontinent.eu, interview with Karola Brede, 18 March 2026

stops.name: Bockenheim, in Habermas's Frankfurt
stops.date_confidence: contradiction flagged, not resolved. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp has said plainly that Karp studied philosophy under Jurgen Habermas and completed the doctorate under him; de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp says Habermas taught him but names Karola Brede as Doktorvater, and en.wikipedia's current text lists Brede as referee. Both language editions therefore support teaching contact and reject the supervision claim. A separate strain is chronological: Habermas held the Frankfurt chair until 1994 and Karp arrived c.1995, so any contact falls at the edge of the tenure or in the emeritus years. No source reached fixes a date, a course, or a seminar. The 1996 date orders the segment only.
stops.campa: Jurgen Habermas teaches him. The claim that Karp took his doctorate under Habermas travels farther and faster than the truth, and profile after profile repeats it; his actual supervisor has said otherwise, on the record, in an interview. What is left when the legend is stripped off is smaller and stranger: an American law graduate with no German, arriving at the far end of the great man's Frankfurt tenure, in the room where communicative action was argued out, and arguing.
suggested_refs: Jurgen Habermas, Theorie des kommunikativen Handelns (1981), the tradition Karp entered from outside
sources: legrandcontinent.eu, interview with Karola Brede, 18 March 2026

stops.name: Myliusstrasse, the Sigmund Freud Institute
stops.date_confidence: de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp places the Sigmund-Freud-Institut research post during his doctoral studies, not after them; a dossier chronology dating it to 2002 is impossible on the same sources' own account, since he left Frankfurt in 2001. The 1998 date is a placement inside the doctoral years and is not attested. The detail that he stood in for Karola Brede's post while she was a visiting professor abroad, and the reading groups on authoritarianism, sociology and psychoanalysis, come from the legrandcontinent.eu Brede interview. Coordinates are Myliusstrasse 20 in the Westend, the institute's home since 14 October 1964; a dossier pin at 50.1178, 8.6717 is about 800 m east of it and is not used.
stops.campa: At the Sigmund Freud Institute on Myliusstrasse he holds a research post and stands in for his supervisor Karola Brede while she is a visiting professor abroad. The work is on authoritarianism, sociology and psychoanalysis, done in reading groups in a Westend house the institute has held since 1964. He is standing in for a post he has not earned yet, in a discipline he came to late, working in his second language. Nothing in the record suggests he means to leave Germany. The groups meet and the dissertation grows.
sources: legrandcontinent.eu, interview with Karola Brede, 18 March 2026

stops.name: Frankfurt, the decision to go back
stops.date_confidence: attested that he left Frankfurt in 2001 after considering staying permanently, and that he went back to the United States for work (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp; de.wikipedia agrees on mid-1990s to 2001). Month and day are defaults. The reason given in the campa is his own retrospective account from the 2025 Economic Club transcript, which is a statement about academia in general and is not tied by him to this departure; the connection is the writer's, and the quote is dated in its own source line.
stops.campa: He has been in Frankfurt roughly six years and considers staying for good. He does not stay. The reason he gives afterward is not homesickness and not money in the first instance: the academy, as he tells it, rewarded politics over being right, and being right in it changed nothing. He goes back to the United States for work in 2001, having spent six years learning to think in a language he did not have when he came. The doctorate is still a year from conferral and there is nothing on the record about what he means to do next.
stops.quote: I left academia because I felt like I was almost always right, and it didn't matter because it was all politics.
stops.quote_source: Economic Club of New York, fireside chat transcript, 24 February 2025 (econclubny.org, official transcript PDF)
sources: Economic Club of New York transcript, 24 February 2025

stops.name: Frankfurt, Aggression in der Lebenswelt
stops.date_confidence: the 2002 doctorate, the full German title, the magna cum laude grade, Karola Brede as first examiner and Hans-Joachim Busch as second are attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp; de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp). Month and day are defaults. Note that he had already left Frankfurt in 2001, so the conferral postdates his residence there; the pin is the institution's, not a documented presence. The German National Library record d-nb.info/966060652/34 returned 404 on the attempt made in this pass, so the dissertation itself was not read.
stops.campa: The doctorate is conferred at Goethe University for a dissertation titled Aggression in der Lebenswelt, which extends Talcott Parsons on aggression by describing how jargon, aggression and culture hold together: how a bounded, specialized language makes a community by keeping other people outside it. Karola Brede is first examiner, Hans-Joachim Busch second. It is graded magna cum laude. It has never been published in English, and the English title in circulation is a journalist's rendering rather than an edition.
suggested_refs: Alexander Karp, Aggression in der Lebenswelt (Goethe University Frankfurt, 2002), untranslated

stops.name: London, the Caedmon Group
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp places the Caedmon Group in London and gives the seed as a twelve thousand dollar inheritance from his paternal grandfather, but the dossier could not establish the firm's domicile, its assets, or its dissolution, and no filing was reached in this pass. Coordinates are a central-London placeholder, not an address. Month and day are defaults.
stops.campa: With twelve thousand dollars inherited from his paternal grandfather he starts the Caedmon Group in London and manages money for European clients. It works well enough that he is financially independent before he is anything else, and that is the condition on which the rest of the life turns: when the offer comes to run a startup nobody has heard of, he does not need it. No filing for the Caedmon Group was reached in any register, so what it held and when it wound up stay unknown.

stops.name: Palo Alto, the Shire: Palantir incorporated
stops.date_confidence: attested to 6 May 2003 with the five named co-founders and the PayPal fraud-detection premise (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palantir_Technologies). Coordinates and the internal name of the Palo Alto office are inherited byte-identical from peter_thiel.journey.json, stop 'Palo Alto, Palantir incorporated', whose campa names Karp explicitly at this pin and date. The exact street address of the earliest office is not confirmed anywhere reached.
stops.campa: Palantir Technologies is incorporated on the sixth of May by Peter Thiel with Stephen Cohen, Joe Lonsdale, Nathan Gettings and Karp, who is not an engineer, has never worked in Silicon Valley, and holds a German doctorate in social theory. The premise is to take the fraud-detection logic PayPal built against Russian card rings and sell it to intelligence agencies instead of to merchants. The office is called the Shire. Karp is thirty-five, and this is his first job in technology.
stops.quote: We were going to build the thing the government ought to want, not what they asked for.
stops.quote_source: Economic Club of New York, fireside chat transcript, 24 February 2025 (econclubny.org, official transcript PDF)
sources: Economic Club of New York transcript, 24 February 2025

stops.name: Palo Alto, In-Q-Tel's two million
stops.date_confidence: attested that In-Q-Tel, the Central Intelligence Agency's venture arm, was among the early investors with roughly two million dollars (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palantir_Technologies). The 2004 date follows that page's account of the formal launch; month and day are defaults. That agency analysts shaped the product is the company's own repeated account and is carried as reconstruction.
stops.campa: In-Q-Tel, the venture arm the Central Intelligence Agency set up to buy its way into commercial technology it could not build itself, puts about two million dollars into the company. The money matters less than what comes with it, which is analysts inside the agency who will use the software and complain about it until it changes. In its second year, a firm run by a self-described socialist with a Frankfurt doctorate in social theory is capitalized in part by American intelligence.
stops.quote: We, at Palantir, want the best thing for this country. That is a true and not plausible statement because obviously I'm a large stakeholder in a company with very specific interests.
stops.quote_source: Economic Club of New York, fireside chat transcript, 24 February 2025 (econclubny.org, official transcript PDF)
sources: Economic Club of New York transcript, 24 February 2025

stops.name: Palo Alto, the chief executive
stops.date_confidence: contradiction flagged, not resolved. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp and en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palantir_Technologies give 2004; company materials cited in the dossier date the formal CEO title to 2005. No board record settling it was reached. Month and day are defaults inside the earlier of the two candidate years.
stops.campa: He becomes chief executive of Palantir. The date is not clean: the encyclopedias say 2004, the company's own materials have said 2005, and nobody has produced the board minute that would settle it. What is not in dispute is the shape of the job, which is to sell to governments a product built by engineers who distrust governments, from inside a valley whose social consensus holds that this kind of work is beneath a serious person. He holds the post for more than twenty years.

stops.name: McLean, Rivendell
stops.date_confidence: the McLean office and its internal name Rivendell are attested (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palantir_Technologies); the mid-2000s dating is the dossier's and the 2006 date orders the segment rather than fixing an opening. In-Q-Tel's own headquarters is in Arlington and Herndon, not McLean, so this pin marks Palantir's office and not the investor's. No source documents how often Karp himself was in the building.
stops.campa: Palantir opens an office in McLean, Virginia, a few miles from the Central Intelligence Agency's headquarters, and calls it Rivendell after the last homely house east of the sea. Palo Alto is the Shire and Virginia is Rivendell; the naming is less a joke the customers are in on than a private map the company keeps of itself. From inside the intelligence community's own suburb it sells that community software named for a seeing stone that shows a watcher anything, at any distance.
suggested_refs: The palantiri of Tolkien's legendarium, the seeing stones that can be turned by a stronger hand

segments.name: Gotham, and the Decade of Contradictions

stops.name: Palo Alto, Gotham
stops.date_confidence: attested that Palantir developed and began deploying Gotham for intelligence, defense and law-enforcement customers, with 2008 as the working date (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palantir_Technologies); month and day are defaults. The bin Laden story is explicitly marked here as unverified legend: no official American after-action record consulted confirms it, moneyweek.com notes it is unclear if it is true, and Karp was never at Abbottabad. It appears in this campa as a legend about the software, not as an event, and no stop is pinned at the compound.
stops.campa: Gotham goes out to the intelligence agencies, the military and the police: a platform that takes the databases an institution has never been able to read together and makes them one searchable object. Analysts stop asking what is in a file and start asking what the files, taken together, imply. A legend attaches itself to the software and will not come off, that it found Osama bin Laden in Abbottabad. Palantir does not discuss its customers' operations. No official American after-action record confirms the story, and moneyweek.com, retelling it, says plainly that it is unclear whether it is true.
suggested_refs: moneyweek.com, 'Alex Karp: can Batman save America', on the bin Laden story and its uncertainty

stops.name: Palo Alto, the apology for HBGary
stops.date_confidence: attested that a Palantir employee was implicated with HBGary Federal and Berico Technologies in a proposal to discredit WikiLeaks supporters and the journalist Glenn Greenwald, and that Karp apologized publicly and severed ties (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palantir_Technologies, corroborating the dossier). The February 2011 dating follows the leak of the documents; the exact day of the apology was not re-verified. The pin is Palantir's own headquarters: HBGary Federal was in Sacramento, and Karp is not documented in that city or anywhere else on the day, so no Sacramento stop is staged for him.
stops.campa: A Palantir engineer is found to have joined HBGary Federal and Berico Technologies in a pitch to discredit supporters of WikiLeaks and the journalist Glenn Greenwald. The whole proposal becomes public when HBGary's mail is broken open and dumped. Nothing in the record shows Karp authorized the pitch or knew of it. He apologizes anyway, in his own name, to Greenwald and to progressives generally, in terms a chief executive's lawyers would ordinarily have hedged, and he cuts the company loose from HBGary.
sources: alex_karp.dossier.md, citing contemporary reporting on the HBGary leak

stops.name: Palo Alto, Foundry and the other customer
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Foundry's existence as the commercial counterpart to Gotham is general Palantir corporate history, but the exact launch year was not pinned down against a primary source in this pass; 2016 is the dossier's working date and is carried as such. The pin is the Palo Alto headquarters of the period, which is where the company still was.
stops.campa: Foundry is built for the other customer, the one that is not a government: banks, manufacturers, hospitals, airlines, institutions drowning in data they cannot join. The same problem, the same shape of answer, a different buyer and a far larger market. Gotham keeps the name that frightens people; Foundry earns the revenue that eventually pays for it. The year the platform actually opens is not fixed by anything reachable here, and 2016 is a working date rather than a fact.

stops.name: Washington, the Department of Labor complaint
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to date and pin. The Department of Labor's allegation that Palantir discriminated against Asian applicants in engineering hiring, and the roughly 1.7 million dollar settlement in 2017 without admission of wrongdoing, come from Department of Labor administrative materials cited in the dossier and from en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp. The September 2016 date orders the segment; the pin is the department's headquarters at 200 Constitution Avenue, not a documented personal visit by Karp, who is not placed in this building on any day by any source.
stops.campa: The Department of Labor brings an administrative complaint alleging that Palantir's engineering hiring discriminated against Asian applicants. The chief executive who talks constantly about meritocracy is answering a federal charge about who his company hires. The proceeding is a paper one; Karp is not documented in this building on any day, and the pin belongs to the department rather than to him. In 2017 the company settles for about 1.7 million dollars and admits no wrongdoing.
sources: alex_karp.dossier.md, citing Department of Labor administrative materials

segments.name: The German Boards and the Break with the Valley

stops.name: Berlin, the Axel Springer supervisory board
stops.date_confidence: attested (de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp): Karp joined the Axel Springer supervisory board, the Aufsichtsrat, in 2018, left it in January 2020, moved to the shareholders' committee, and served until that committee was dissolved in 2025. en.wikipedia gives director 2018 to 2020 and shareholders committee 2022 to 2025, so the two editions disagree on whether the committee service was continuous from 2020 or resumed in 2022; that contradiction is flagged, not resolved. Aufsichtsrat and Vorstand are distinct organs in a German SE and he was never on the second. Month and day are defaults. The coordinates sit a few hundred metres east of the Axel-Springer-Strasse complex and no exact figure was confirmed from a fetched source; treat the pin as approximate.
stops.campa: He joins the supervisory board of Axel Springer in Berlin, the publishing house of Bild and Die Welt. It is an Aufsichtsrat seat and not a management one; in a German company the two organs are separate and he never sits on the second. Germany is not a phase he left behind. He keeps the second language, the second country and a set of German institutional obligations for a quarter of a century after the doctorate. In January 2020 he leaves the board for the shareholders' committee, which is dissolved in 2025.

stops.name: Palo Alto, the socialist who does not follow his friend
stops.date_confidence: attested that Karp publicly identifies as a socialist and a progressive, states he voted for the Democratic candidate in 2016, and did not follow Peter Thiel into support for Donald Trump (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp). No date or venue attaches to the statements as a group; 2018 and the Palo Alto pin place them where he and the company then were, and both are editorial placements. The quote is from 2025 and is dated in its own source line.
stops.campa: He says publicly that he is a socialist and a progressive, that he voted for the Democratic candidate in 2016, and that he is not following his oldest friend into the Trump camp. Thiel has gone the other way and gone loudly, and the two of them do not stop speaking. The position costs Karp nothing inside Palantir and most of his credibility with the left he claims, which does not believe a defense contractor can hold it. He goes on holding it in public for another six years.
stops.quote: I think I'm the only last real progressive. Yeah, I believe in progress.
stops.quote_source: Economic Club of New York, fireside chat transcript, 24 February 2025 (econclubny.org, official transcript PDF)
sources: Economic Club of New York transcript, 24 February 2025

stops.name: Ludwigshafen am Rhein, the BASF supervisory board
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day (de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp): appointed to the BASF supervisory board on 3 May 2019, departed July 2020. A dossier chronology treating the German board roles as vaguely 2010s, and treating the Axel Springer role as ending in 2020, is corrected here: only the BASF role ends then. Coordinates are the city of Ludwigshafen, not the BASF works complex north of the centre; the pin is town-level.
stops.campa: He is appointed to the supervisory board of BASF, the chemical concern at Ludwigshafen on the Rhine, on the third of May. He serves fourteen months and is gone by July 2020. The two German boards, Springer and BASF, are the visible part of a life that keeps one foot in Europe while the company he runs turns into an instrument of American state power. He gives up the chemical company in the same season his own company moves its headquarters out of California.

stops.name: Denver, the headquarters moved
stops.date_confidence: attested to August 2020, with Karp framing the move as distance from Silicon Valley's engineering elite (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palantir_Technologies); the day is a default. The street address at 1200 17th Street is from general public record and was not independently re-verified. The quote is from 2025 and is dated in its own source line.
stops.campa: Palantir moves its headquarters from Palo Alto to Denver. Karp gives the reason in public and does not soften it: the monoculture of the engineering elite in Silicon Valley, its settled consensus about which work is respectable, and the plain fact that his company's work is not. The move is read as theater by people who assume a headquarters is only an address. Palantir has been in Palo Alto for seventeen years, and after August 2020 the company's registered home is Colorado.
stops.quote: There is nothing noble in embracing values and ideas that have never worked.
stops.quote_source: Economic Club of New York, fireside chat transcript, 24 February 2025 (econclubny.org, official transcript PDF)
sources: Economic Club of New York transcript, 24 February 2025

stops.name: New York Stock Exchange, the direct listing
stops.date_confidence: attested to 30 September 2020, a direct listing under the ticker PLTR with a three-class share structure preserving founder control for Karp, Thiel and Cohen (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palantir_Technologies, and SEC filings cited in the dossier). Coordinates are inherited byte-identical from peter_thiel.journey.json, stop 'New York Stock Exchange, Palantir direct-lists', whose campa names Karp at this pin and date.
stops.campa: Seventeen years after incorporation the company lists directly on the exchange, without underwriters, under the ticker PLTR. The registration discloses a three-class share structure whose Class F shares keep voting control with Karp, Thiel and Cohen whatever fraction of the equity they actually hold. The self-described socialist takes a company public on terms that make its founders effectively unremovable; both halves of that sentence are documented in the same filing. The company has never yet reported a profitable year.
sources: peter_thiel.journey.json, stop 'New York Stock Exchange, Palantir direct-lists'

stops.name: Denver, the billion-dollar year
stops.date_confidence: attested that his reported 2020 compensation was approximately 1.1 billion dollars, overwhelmingly long-dated stock options, making him one of the highest-compensated public-company executives of the year (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alex_Karp). The 31 December date closes the fiscal year and is a device. The eleven houses and the Lyman residence are attested on the same page but are undated there; they are mentioned here as context and pinned properly at their own stop.
stops.campa: His reported compensation for the year is about 1.1 billion dollars, nearly all of it long-dated options rather than cash, which puts him among the highest-paid executives of any public company in America. Options are not money until somebody exercises them, and this figure counts them as money years before that. The grants are long-dated and the price has to hold.
